The metal torus is modeled as a perfectly electrically conducting, impenetrable body embedded in a lossless, homogeneous, isotropic medium with zero conductivity.
The incident electromagnetic fields are generated by a time-harmonic magnetic dipole of arbitrary orientation located near the torus.
Electromagnetic fields are expanded in positive integral powers of the real wave number k of the exterior medium at low frequencies.
Only the static Rayleigh term (n=0) and the first three dynamic terms (n=1,2,3) are retained for the solution; terms for n≥4 are neglected.
The scattering problem reduces to coupled boundary value problems involving Laplace and Poisson equations with perfectly conducting boundary conditions on the torus surface.
The scattered magnetic field at order n=0 satisfies an uncoupled Laplace equation with no scattered electric field at this order.
At order n=1, the scattered electric field is vector harmonic with zero scattered magnetic field.
At order n=2, the scattered magnetic field satisfies a Poisson equation coupled to the n=0 term, with no scattered electric field.
At order n=3, both scattered magnetic and electric fields appear; the magnetic field satisfies a Laplace equation, while the electric field requires an integral representation solution.
The scattered fields are expressed as infinite series expansions in standard toroidal harmonic eigenfunctions.
Boundary conditions enforce cancellation of the normal component of the total magnetic field and tangential component of the total electric field on the torus surface.
Silver–Müller radiation conditions are imposed at infinity to ensure physically correct scattered field behavior.
Toroidal coordinates (η, θ, φ) are introduced to fit the torus geometry exactly, with parameters a (overall radius) and b (torus opening).
The wave number k is related to the circular frequency ω and medium parameters permittivity ε and permeability μ by k = ω√(εμ).
The low-frequency expansions reveal that the incident magnetic field has no dynamic term at n=1, while the incident electric field has no static term at n=0.
The infinite linear systems for unknown coefficients are solved approximately by truncation and standard numerical linear algebra techniques.
The scattered magnetic field is complex-valued, while the scattered electric field is purely imaginary in the low-frequency approximation.
The problem formulation excludes the singular dipole source point from the scattering domain to avoid interface phenomena.
The torus is centered on the x3-axis with symmetry axis aligned accordingly in the toroidal coordinate system.
The analytical solutions provide a foundation for forward scattering problems and can assist in inverse problem algorithms for anomaly detection.
